Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

comprehensive adjective

also comprehensively, thorough (covering everything), all-round, full (a full account), complete (covering everything)

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.4.57: omnia alicujus facta ōrātiōne (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Brut. 14: omnium rērum memoriam breviter librō (Lewis & Short)

omnia complectēns

complector, complectī, complexus sum, deponent, with accusative; in a relative clause, quī omnia complectitur

taking in everything: comprehensive

Latin has no adjective for it: a comprehensive account is one that embraces everything, quae omnia complectitur. Complector is to embrace, and so to take in a subject whole, in thought or in a book.

Other words

  • ūniversus, ūniversa, ūniversum — whole, all together, general

    declension · also used · classical

    Of the whole taken together, against its parts (ūniversa rēs, the whole subject); for a comprehensive view, not a comprehensive account.

Examples

  • Hic liber omnia complectitur quae ad hortōs colendōs pertinent.

    This book is comprehensive: it covers everything to do with gardening.composed

See also total, whole, carefully, perfect.

SourcesLewis & Short: complector · Lewis & Short: universus
